newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar mixed, March captures volume.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar mixed, March captures volume.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE white sugar futures were mixed in choppy trade on Monday afternoon with the March contract capturing most of the day's buying, traders said.
Trading conditions calmed down after early activity in the Dec/March spread, which narrowed to around $2.50 by 1645 GMT after ranging between $2.70 and $4.40, traders said.

Outright activity centred on March which stood 80 cents higher at $306.00 a tonne after a session high of $306.80, while December was 20 cents lower at $308.00 after a high of $309.90. Volume reached 1,881 lots.
Traders said there were no fresh physical demand news to stir activity.
The market is oversold and some analysts said although a bounce from the lows is not out of the question, recent movements suggest prices could continue to consolidate before easing further.
"It's just bouncing technically since we've been going down in the last few weeks. But I'm not overly bearish," said one trader.
This week sees the deadline for bids in Syria's tender to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws for Nov/Dec shipment. Results are expected on November 6.
On the charts, analysts pegged the immediate support at $303.70 basis March and resistance at $310.00, followed by $311.80.
Paris positions were also mixed, with March sugar rising 10 cents at $305.50. New York was slightly down.

In other news, an official in Poland said the country could export some 400,000 tonnes of sugar without subsidies next year as its beet campaign is likely to result in record sugar output of 2.1 million tonnes this year.
